### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2c5283e3a2c664f4e09dbe6115abe913e5e1ef1b` — the merge of head `82cc3c1593afa70f3367cd72029bc7232c0fb199` into base `b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2c5283e3a2c664f4e09dbe6115abe913e5e1ef1b && git checkout 2c5283e3a2c664f4e09dbe6115abe913e5e1ef1b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a 82cc3c1593afa70f3367cd72029bc7232c0fb199 && git checkout -B drift-repro b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a && git merge --no-ff 82cc3c1593afa70f3367cd72029bc7232c0fb199

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b392ff7bdf4c470d422bc8723aa46dc3e301b87a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

N1 fixed (predicate → `boolean`, the one narrowing caller now goes through `isPackageScopedType`). N3 measured SAME before and after every hydration path (boot load, list read, bare-slot copies; one and two holders, both orders), so nothing changes for N3; the boot load joins the existing location-4 pins. Declared `Clause-②: no` for the .d.ts return-type change — please judge.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4bb529d89e4bc071c81e6f6f68a63a1562490ed5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, .changeset/32716-judges-package-less-rows-boolean.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/stored-package-references.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **The fix is right.** `judgesPackageLessRows` returns `false` for a package-scoped type the registry does not read by package (`hook`), so `type is PackageScopedType` narrowed that type to `never` in a caller's `false` branch. That is unsound. Returning `boolean` removes it. The one in-repo caller that relied on the narrowing (`packageLessRowOwners`) now narrows with `isPackageScopedType`, whose answer depends only on the type, before asking. The runtime answer of both functions is unchanged. The other caller (`cli/stored-package-references.ts`, a `filter` over `PACKAGE_SCOPED_TYPES`) does not use the narrowing. The tsc pin plus its ablation measure it.
- **N3 measured the same, and the new pins add the boot load.** A package-less sealed-type row read at a holder's exact address answers the holder's own item before and after `loadMetaFromDb`, around the list hydrator, and with a bare-slot copy, for one holder and for two. No read moves.
- **must-fix M1: the declaration (your question).** `Clause-②: no` does not hold. `judgesPackageLessRows` is exported from `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (`index.ts`), and its declared return type is public surface. A caller that wrote `if (judgesPackageLessRows(registry, t)) usePackageScoped(t)` compiled before, because the `true` branch narrowed soundly. At this head it does not compile. That shrinks what the published package exposes, which is the narrowing arm (CONTRIBUTING, Human Minimum item 5: "accept set or public surface"; the same reading review#1 gave on #33121: refusing something a caller could write before is a narrowing). Declare `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, add `!` to the title, add a short **BREAKING** paragraph (who: a TypeScript caller that narrowed through this function; fix: call `isPackageScopedType` from `@objectstack/core` first, which your changeset already says), and add one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. The level stays `patch`: this is a non-protocol change, and `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. A delta that changes only that text converts this to PASS.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` is correct for a non-protocol narrowing. The declaration is M1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- First-party reach is nil: no in-repo caller narrows through the `true` branch any more. The narrowing lands only on an external TypeScript consumer, and only at compile time. Nothing changes at runtime.
- The PR is a draft with CI running (read 22:40Z). The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head. As a narrowing arm, it also owes the dogfood battery.

### ④ Design judgment

Dropping an unsound predicate rather than keeping a half-right one is the right call. TypeScript has no one-sided predicate, and a predicate that lies in its `false` branch is worse than none. Moving the narrowing onto `isPackageScopedType` at the one caller keeps every type-only answer type-only. The design holds. The FAIL is the declaration only.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
